reason: While King Josiah is the central figure exercising significant agency in directing religious reforms, the text clearly depicts multiple non-leaders exercising agency throughout. The workers (עֹשֵׂי הַמְּלָאכָה) demonstrate agency through faithful labor (בֶאֱמוּנָה הֵם עֹשִׂים). Most significantly, 'the people of the land' (עַם־הָאָרֶץ) exercise political agency by choosing and anointing the new king (v. 23:30: וַיִּקַּח עַם־הָאָרֶץ אֶת־יְהֽוֹאָחָז), and 'all the people' (כָּל־הָעָם) exercise religious agency by standing in the covenant with the Lord (v. 23:3: וַיַּעֲמֹד כָּל־הָעָם בַּבְּרִֽית). These passages demonstrate that common people make real choices and take consequential actions, establishing that agency extends beyond leaders.
